title: Repro matrix: driver + firmware + RNG variance (performance causality notes)
content:
Purpose:
This note collects ad-hoc experiments exploring non-deterministic performance variance across driver versions, GPU firmware revisions, and internal RNG seeds that affect micro-benchmarks and end-to-end token latency in the serving runtime. The goal is to build a reproducibility matrix and actionable mitigations for noisy signals in our CI and production telemetry.

High-level hypothesis / motivation:
- We observe persistent but small (1–12%) fluctuations in p50/p95 token latency and throughput that are not explained by clear load or scheduling differences.
- Suspect contributors: GPU driver version, GPU firmware (microcode) revision, CUDA runtime version, and subtle interactions with the host kernel scheduler (cpu frequency scaling, IRQ affinity) and library RNG seeds used by libraries (cuBLAS, custom kernels).
- Need to know which combinations are stable enough to use as baselines for regression detection.

Experiment matrix (summary):
- Hardware: A100 40GB (n1-standard), H100 80GB (n1-standard), L40S 48GB (n2-standard)
- Cloud SKUs: us-west1, us-east4, europe-west3 (same GPU sku different host firmware pushes)
- Driver versions tested: 515.105, 520.61, 525.89, 535.86 (representative vendor pushes)
- CUDA runtimes: 11.8, 12.0, 12.1
- Firmware: captured GPU microcode ids (where available) using nvidia-smi -q --verbose
- RNG modes: library-default, fixed-seed (42) everywhere, and kernel-randomized (fresh boot between runs)
- Workloads: small-batch single-token decode (prefill 1+decode 1), long-context 8k prefill+decode, KV-cache heavy workload with repeated prefixes

Methodology notes:
- Each cell in the matrix is 30 trials across a 30-minute window. We collect per-trial p50/p90/p99, CPU pinning state, IRQ affinity summary, and full nvidia-smi sampling at 1s.
- To isolate driver/firmware effects we hold host kernel (Ubuntu 22.04, 5.15) constant where possible and reboot between driver installs.
- For firmware variants we used cloud-hosted images that expose different microcode bundles (observed in different regions). When possible, we recorded the ROM version string from nvidia-smi.
- We instrumented the runtime to emit per-token timing and kernel launch timestamps (host monotonic ns) to allow correlation.

Key observations (aggregated):
1) Driver major releases introduce coherent shifts in p50/p95: 520.x -> 525.x often shifted p95 by +6–9% on H100 for small-batch decode workloads while p50 moved by only ~1–2%. This suggests fewer large outliers but more mid-level jitter (kernel scheduling/latency amplification).

2) Firmware (ROM/microcode) differences are correlated with occasional, reproducible multi-second stalls at the tail when combined with certain driver/OS combos. These stalls appear as spaced spikes (one every ~200–500 trials) and are strongly region dependent — identical GPU SKU but different host image/firmware produced different spike rates.

3) RNG/fixed-seed experiments: using a fixed internal RNG seed for our custom CUDA kernels reduced variance in microbenchmarks (matmul/memory-copy microprofiling) by ~20% of observed stddev, but had negligible effect on end-to-end p99 in full runtime workloads. Interpretation: stochastic kernel paths contribute to numeric noise but are not the primary cause of performance tails at the E2E level.

4) CUDA runtime version changes (11.8 -> 12.x) introduced observable differences in kernel-launch batching behavior and cuBLAS heuristics. On A100 we saw a slight improvement in throughput with 12.1 for long-context workloads, but on L40S the new runtime sometimes regressed p99 by ~5% depending on driver combo.

5) Host-level scheduling & IRQ affinity: when IRQs for NVHPC/NVLINK were pinned away from the main CPU thread the p99 tail reduced on average by 8% for small-batch workloads. This correlates with fewer CPU kernel-launch delays observed in perf traces.

6) Reboots matter: many “noisy” cells became substantially more stable after a full host reboot post-driver/firmware change. Hot-driver swaps produced higher variance.

Detailed examples / anomaly traces:
- H100, driver 525.89, CUDA 12.0, firmware v1.2.4: repeated 3–4s stalls every ~300 runs. Stack traces captured in kernel logs at time of stall showed NVLINK/FW microcode handshake warnings. Rebooted host and re-ran: spikes disappeared for 2k runs then reappeared after another ~24 hours of baseline traffic.

- A100, driver 520.61, CUDA 11.8: consistent p50/p95 but occasional 150–300ms tail attributed to CPU frequency governor switching under low-load test bench. Locking CPU freq to performance governor removed these tails.

Practical recommendations (short-term):
- CI baseline picking: pin a specific driver + CUDA runtime + recorded firmware id per hardware line and require that regression detection compare only within that matrix cell. If we must compare across cells, include an uncertainty buffer derived from observed intra-cell variance.
- During driver rollouts: require a canary bucket in region+sku combos for 72 hours and force full reboot on driver install before measurement. Avoid hot-swap driver updates in production without reboot and stability window.
- Production telemetry: instrument and emit firmware ROM id and driver version as top-level request metadata so downstream alerting can group by exact binary surface.
- Mitigations for tail-outliers: IRQ pinning for NV drivers, lock CPU frequency during sensitive latency windows, and consider a tiny jitter-expunging warmup phase that performs a small GPU busy-loop before accepting traffic to settle firmware/driver state.
- RNG and determinism: keep fixed-seed kernel mode for microbench regression tests, but do not rely on it for E2E tests. For numeric determinism tests keep a separate deterministic CI lane.

Follow-ups / open questions:
- Need to catalogue region images to identify where host firmware mismatches consistently produce microcode-related spikes.
- Evaluate whether vendor-supplied firmware updates contain timing-affecting patches; coordinate with cloud partners for change notifications.
- Quantify effect of host kernel upgrades (5.15 -> 6.x) paired with driver updates — we only held kernel constant in these runs, but production images vary.
- Add telemetry for per-request IRQ affinity and kernel launch timestamp correlation to trace and automatically triage the root cause when tails occur.

Appendix: short checklist for re-running these experiments
- Fresh VM per driver install; capture full dmesg and nvidia-smi -q output before/after.
- Use fixed experiment harness container that stamps monotonic time in logs and uploads trace artifacts to S3 with naming convention: repro/<date>/<gpu>/<driver>/<firmware>/<seed>.tgz
- Run 30 trials per cell over 30 minutes, collect p50/p90/p99, and attach perf samples at CPU-level and NVTX markers in the runtime for the prefill + decode phase.

Notes to self:
- This doc is a living scratchpad. Convert to a proper runbook if results are validated across more regions. Capture the firmware strings and attach example trace tarballs to the GH issue linked above.

-- Evan
